issues.description: Nil-receiver guards are scattered ad hoc across every accessor instead of decomposed into one place
issues.detail: The same pattern — `var slice T; if f != nil { slice = f.field }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(slice, ...)` — is open-coded in ~12 methods across ir_file.go, ir_imports.go, ir_type.go. That is incidental complexity: the concern 'a nil/zero handle yields an empty view' is one idea, repeated. A small helper (e.g. `safeSlice(f, func(f *File) []id.ID[T] { ... })`) or, better, separating the *value* (the slice descriptor) from the *identity* (the *File handle) would let one place express 'zero handle -> zero value' instead of every getter knowing about it.

issues.description: Two different zero-encodings (nil pointer and IsZero() value) are complected behind one API
issues.detail: Some types are accessed via nil pointer receivers (`*File`, `*imports`), others via value receivers with `IsZero()` (`Member`, `Type`, `Oneof`, `Element`, `ReservedName`). The PR now teaches every method to handle whichever flavor its receiver happens to use. That's two distinct notions of 'absence' intertwined with the accessor surface. Pick one model — value types with IsZero, or nilable pointers — and push the absence check to construction/wrapping, not into every leaf method. Right now the IR is place-oriented in some spots and value-oriented in others, and callers must know which.

issues.description: Reflection-based test is testing the test infrastructure, not the invariant
issues.detail: `testZeroAny` walks methods by reflection and asserts 'returns a zero value or has Len()==0'. This is TDD-as-design in reverse: instead of stating the invariant ('a zero handle behaves as an empty file with no members'), it iterates whatever methods happen to exist and applies special cases (`ValueNodeIndex` returns -1, `Context` must be assignable to *ir.File, indexers get unwrapped via `Len`). New methods get auto-covered with a generic 'zero-ish' assertion that may not match what 'zero' should mean for that method. A table of explicit expectations per accessor — even a long one — would test the actual contract rather than 'whatever the code returns today, that's the spec.'

issues.description: `IsAny` zero-guard added but other Type predicates that touch session were not audited
issues.detail: `Type.IsAny` is guarded with `!t.IsZero() && ...` but the parallel `File.IsDescriptorProto` was fixed via `f == nil`. Same essential concern (predicate on a zero/nil receiver that dereferences session/builtins), two different fixes. Worth a pass to find the rest of the predicates on Type/File/Member/etc. that still panic — the test is broad but the fix is local, so coverage of 'all session-touching predicates' is implicit, not stated.

issues.description: `Element.ValueNodeIndex` overloads the return type to signal absence
issues.detail: Returning -1 from a method whose name implies 'an index' complects 'index value' with 'presence bit'. Every caller now has to remember 'oh and -1 means zero element'. A separate `Ok()` / two-value return, or making the doc and signature `(int, bool)`, would keep value and presence as separate concerns. Minor because the doc does say so, but it's the same complecting pattern in miniature.

issues.description: `Imports.Transitive` slice expression is duplicated, easy to drift
issues.detail: `i.files[:max(0, len(i.files)-1)]` is computed inside the nil-guarded branch, and the 'exclude the implicit descriptor.proto' invariant lives both here and in `DescriptorProto`. If the encoding of 'descriptor.proto is the last entry' changes, three call sites must change together. A named accessor on `*imports` (e.g. `directsAndTransitives()` returning two slices) would keep that invariant in one place.

review.summary: The PR does a useful thing — zero values shouldn't panic — but the *way* it does it is COMPLECTED. The same 'guard then read' pattern is open-coded across roughly a dozen accessors, and the codebase now carries two different notions of 'absence' (nil pointer for File/imports, IsZero() for value types) that callers and every getter must keep straight. That's INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY: the essential idea is 'a zero handle yields an empty view,' and it should live in one place — either by separating the value (slice descriptor) from the identity (*File handle), or via a small helper that all accessors funnel through. The reflection-based test is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: it covers a lot of surface cheaply, but it tests 'whatever methods return today' rather than the stated invariant, with special cases hardcoded for the methods that don't fit. The question that should have been asked first: 'what does a zero IR mean, and where does that meaning live?' — answered once, it removes most of the per-method edits in this diff.
